title: Local splitting after a surjective degree-zero fibre map
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $K$ be a perfect object of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_S)$ [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex] whose Tor-amplitude is in $[0,\infty)$. Fix a point $s\in S$ and suppose that the canonical map $H^0(K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_S}\kappa(s)\to H^0(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_S}\kappa(s))$ is surjective. Then there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $s$ and an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_U)$, $K|_U\cong H^0(K)|_U\oplus P$, where $P$ is perfect of Tor-amplitude in $[1,\infty)$.

proof.text: At s take a strictly perfect local model of K and refine it to a bounded finite-free model on an affine open. Lift that complex through fully faithful affine sheafification, choosing the free module of each finite rank and conjugating/lifting its differentials. Faithfulness proves square-zero and transfers the upper bound. This gives the bounded-above finite-free module complex needed for the affine cut.

proof.text: Realize the supplied algebraic splitting on an open neighbourhood, obtaining a positive perfect sheaf summand and the canonical nonpositive truncation as the other summand.

source.place: Tag 0A1U, Lemma better-cut-complex-in-two, affine reduction and conclusion

proof.text: Tensor the K-flat witness of negative tensor vanishing with the unit sheaf. The tensor unitor proves that K has no negative homology. Exact open restriction preserves this. The nonpositive truncation is consequently concentrated in degree zero; its H^0 is H^0(K) restricted to the open, by exactness of restriction. The standard derived-category single-functor identification gives the required splitting.
